title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
Waymo's autonomous vehicles were deployed into extreme traffic conditions they were not designed to handle. Multiple vehicles became stranded when Fourth of July gridlock prevented movement long enough to completely drain their batteries. The company's response was reactive, requiring roadside assistance to tow the vehicles rather than preventing the outcome through route planning or pre-event preparation.

This reveals a deployment gap between the conditions a system is tested in and the conditions it encounters in the world. Waymo operates in San Francisco year-round but did not anticipate or prepare for predictable seasonal events that create traffic volumes beyond normal operation. A human dispatch system checking weather, local events, and traffic predictions before releasing vehicles into service that day could have identified the risk.

It is not established whether this represents a failure in the autonomous driving system itself, or whether human operators should have chosen not to deploy vehicles during this event.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
During Fourth of July celebrations in San Francisco on Saturday, multiple Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded in heavy traffic following a fireworks display near the Golden Gate Bridge. At least a dozen vehicles, many of them Jaguar I-PACE models, had their batteries drain completely while stuck in the congestion. The company attributed the problem to major traffic disruptions, high volumes of travelers, and unexpected road closures. Waymo's roadside assistance team had to tow the vehicles away, and the company stated it is evaluating ways to improve its resilience during severe traffic events.

The incident caused frustration among other drivers stuck in the area. Some motorists waited nearly two hours in standstill traffic and reported yelling at the driverless cars. Additionally, one Waymo vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks that someone had set off on the street, though no injuries were reported. Mayor Daniel Lurie's office announced plans to meet with public and private partners to improve traffic management for future events after more than 100,000 people experienced delays leaving the area.
